rows.evidence: Q1: Methodology/Case Study <U+2013> authors run their own coupled MIKESHE/MIKE 11 model of the Mosuowan irrigation district, calibrated (Jan<U+2013>Aug 2006) and tested (Sep<U+2013>Dec 2006) against observed groundwater depths at 10 sites (Fig. 3, Table 2, E=0.77/0.89). Q2: Results 'Effect of Irrigation Methods on Groundwater Recharge Intensity' and Fig. 4 <U+2013> simulated daily recharge was higher under flood irrigation (peaks 0.57 and 0.47 mm/d) than under water-saving irrigation (max 0.42, min 0.1 mm/d); authors conclude water-saving irrigation weakens recharge intensity; the introduction equates water-saving irrigation with drip irrigation; model output was compared with measured groundwater depths from the same district. Q6: Case Study/Fig. 5 <U+2013> effect reported for the whole irrigation district (~4.51<U+00D7>10^4 ha), with 10.22% of district area showing decreased recharge intensity, mainly in farming areas.
rows.notes: Technology doubt: the simulated 2006<U+2013>07 period is labelled 'water-saving irrigation'; drip is named only in the introduction as the water-saving method, so drip is implied rather than explicitly stated for the simulation. The flood (1991<U+2013>92) and water-saving (2006<U+2013>07) periods are different years, so climate and land-use change are confounded with irrigation method; validation was only against 2006 observations. Q3: single modelling method; Moran's I and ArcGIS mapping are analyses of the same model output, not independent evidence. Q4: the model implicitly computes infiltration, but the paper does not report applied water or infiltration/deep percolation as an intermediate variable; the reduced-infiltration explanation is asserted. Q5: one district, one main crop (cotton). Q7: explanations (larger irrigated area with unchanged supply; land-use change; elevation gradient) are not stated as requirements. Q8: no limitations of own result stated; general caveats on numerical models appear only in the introduction. Q9: 5<U+2013>95% bounds, E, R and RMSE are validation metrics; monthly max/min recharge values are temporal variation, not an uncertainty or dispersion measure for the flood-vs-drip difference.

notes: Full text appears complete (pp. 266<U+2013>273). The study is a calibrated distributed hydrological model simulation comparing flood irrigation (1991<U+2013>92) with water-saving (drip-type) irrigation (2006<U+2013>07) in the Mosuowan district, Manasi Basin, China.
